rules.source: Act of 1 August 2018 on the organisation of the National Data Protection Commission and the general data protection framework (Mémorial A No 686 of 16 August 2018) — https://cnpd.public.lu/dam-assets/fr/legislation/droit-lux/Act-of-1-August-2018-on-the-organisation-of-the-National-Data-Protection-Commission-and-the-general-data-protection-framework.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Official text describes the CNPD as an independent public institution with legal personality, financially and administratively autonomous; law-firm summaries state the Act repealed the law of 2 August 2002, derogates from the GDPR for research and statistics and bars processing of genetic data for certain insurance and employment purposes. Consolidated text and later amendments not checked.

rules.source: Penal Code Article 509-1 (fraudulent access to or remaining in an automated data processing or transmission system) — Police grand-ducale https://police.public.lu/en/legislation/infractions-en-matiere-informatique.html
rules.retrieved_snippet: Police summary: fraudulent access carries imprisonment of two months to two years, a fine of EUR 500 to 25,000, or both; an aggravated form applies where data is deleted or changed or the system disrupted; the cybercrime section (Articles 509-1 to 509-7) dates from a 1993 law. Current consolidated text on legilux not checked.

rules.source: Code de la consommation (Consumer Code), including Book 4 on out-of-court consumer dispute resolution added by the law of 17 February 2016 (Mémorial A No 60 of 14 April 2016) — https://cssf.lu/wp-content/uploads/L_170216_Code_consommation.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Article L. 010-1 defines a consumer as a natural person acting outside their commercial, industrial, craft or liberal activity; the Code originated in a 2008 bill that also transposed Directive 2005/29/EC on unfair commercial practices; a bill amending the Code (No 8255) was filed on 27 June 2023 (adoption status not found). Current consolidated text not verified.
